statement.p: A fluid moves through a tube of length 1 meter and radius r = 0.006 \pm 0.00025 meters under a pressure p = 2\cdot 10^5 \pm 1500 pascals, at a rate v= 0.375 \cdot 10^{-9} \hbox{m}^3 per unit time. Use differentials to estimate the maximum error in the viscosity \eta given by \eta = \frac{ \pi}{8} \frac{p r^4}{v}.

static.solution:
\eta is approximated by d\eta, where d\eta = \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial r} dr + \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial p} dp.
We need to find \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial r}=\frac{ \pi}{8} \frac{p 4 r^3}{v } and \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial p}=\frac{ \pi}{8} \frac{ r^4}{v}. For r = 0.006, v = 0.375\cdot 10^{-9} and p=2\cdot 10^5 we get \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial r}(0.006,2\cdot 10^5) = \frac{ \pi}{8} \frac{(2\cdot 10^5)(4\, (0.006)^3)}{0.375\cdot 10^{-9}} = 1.80956\times 10^{8}, and similarly \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial p}(0.006, 2\cdot 10^5) = 1.35717, so that d\eta = \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial r} d r + \frac{\partial \eta}{\partial p} dp. is largest when we take all positive values to give d\eta = (1.80956\times 10^{8})(0.00025) + (1.35717)(1500) = 47274.7.
This seems quite large, but \eta(0.006,2\cdot 10^5) = 271434, so the maximum error represents about 20 % of any value computed by the given formula. Notice also the relative error in r is \pm 4 %, which means that the relative error in r^4 is \pm 10 %.
